flawed_step: Line 0678 (and the identical constant asserted in the statement at line 0626, the reduction at line 0672, and propagated to Corollary item (iv) at line 0710): the claimed Gaussian-integral identity \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{0} \exp(-(\alpha-t)^2/2)\,dt = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{erf}(-\sqrt{2}\alpha).
counterexample:
Take alpha = 1 (a fixed complex/real number allowed by Lemma 'Taylor asymptotics'). With erf defined in the text (line 0610) as erf(z) = (2/sqrt(pi)) * int_0^z e^{-t^2} dt:

LHS: substitute u = alpha - t = 1 - t (du = -dt); as t runs from -infinity to 0, u runs from +infinity down to 1, so
  (1/sqrt(2*pi)) * int_{-inf}^{0} exp(-(1-t)^2/2) dt = (1/sqrt(2*pi)) * int_{1}^{inf} exp(-u^2/2) du = 1 - Phi(1) = 0.1586553...
Equivalently, putting u = sqrt(2) s gives (1/2)(1 - erf(1/sqrt(2))) = (1/2)(1 - 0.6826895) = 0.1586553.

RHS as claimed: (1/2) + (1/2) erf(-sqrt(2)*1) = (1/2)(1 - erf(1.4142136)) = (1/2)(1 - 0.9544997) = 0.0227501.

0.1586553 != 0.0227501, so the asserted identity is false. The correct change of variables gives erf(-alpha/sqrt(2)), not erf(-sqrt(2)*alpha); the two agree only at alpha = 0.

Consequence and independent cross-check: the constant is used verbatim, so Lemma 'Taylor asymptotics' (iii) should read e^{-z} sum_{j<n} z^j/j! = 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-alpha/sqrt(2)) + o(1), and Corollary (iv) should read 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-(z_1 conj(w_2) + w_1 conj(z_2))/sqrt(2)) = (1/2) erfc((z_1 conj(w_2) + w_1 conj(z_2))/sqrt(2)). With z_1 = z_2 = 1 the latter is (1/2) erfc((w_1 + conj(w_2))/sqrt(2)), which is exactly the known Ginibre edge kernel factor; the text's (1/2) erfc(sqrt(2)(w_1 + conj(w_2))) is not. So the stated edge asymptotics for K_n (and hence Lemma 'kernel' derived from it at lines 0717-0718) carry the wrong argument scaling by a factor of 2.
reasoning_summary: Working counterexample-first, I targeted the most concretely checkable claim in the excerpt: the closed-form Gaussian integral at the end of the proof of Lemma 'Taylor asymptotics' (line 0678), since every other step in that proof (Stirling at 0656, the Taylor expansion j(log(1+(z-j)/j) - (z-j)/j) = -(1+o(1))(z-j)^2/(2j) at 0662, and the substitution j = n + sqrt(n) t at 0673-0674 giving exponent -(alpha-t)^2/2) checks out and feeds into it. Evaluating the integral with the text's own definition of erf (line 0610) gives (1/2)(1 - erf(alpha/sqrt(2))), i.e. 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-alpha/sqrt(2)), whereas the text asserts 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-sqrt(2) alpha). At alpha = 1 the true value is 0.158655 and the claimed value is 0.022750. This is not a cosmetic typo: the same wrong constant is carried in the lemma statement (0626), in the reduction target (0672), and into Corollary item (iv) (0710), which is the paper's edge-kernel asymptotic; the corrected constant reproduces the standard Ginibre edge kernel factor (1/2) erfc((w_1 + conj(w_2))/sqrt(2)) while the text's does not. I stopped here per the counterexample-first protocol and did not audit the remaining sections (the swapping/moment argument at 0253-0364 or the resolvent bounds at 0460-0600), both of which looked internally consistent in the parts I read.
